name: execute_command
description: Start a shell command. Destructive, privilege-escalation, remote-shell, and network-listener commands are blocked; ordinary HTTP clients and package managers are allowed. Truncated output reports shown/total counts; narrow or page instead of rerunning variants. Failures report the exit code. Use `yield_time_ms` only for servers, REPLs, or commands that need stdin; builds and tests should use the blocking path so they finish in one call.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for later execute_command calls in this turn:
- Servers, REPLs, and multi-step interactive commands: start with `yield_time_ms` (5000-60000, default 30000), then use `command_session` with action=poll/write/close. Prefer this over `&` plus log-file polling.
- Finite work (builds, tests, formatters): omit `yield_time_ms` and let the call block up to `timeout` (default 60s, max 300s). Do not start a session just because a command is slow: each `command_session` poll is a full model round.
- Polling waits at least 5000ms; do not poll in a tight loop, and never add `sleep` to wait for output. Use `task_wait` for subagent tasks.

command.description: Shell command to start. Servers, REPLs, and multi-step interactive work should use `yield_time_ms`; finite commands should rely on the 60-300s blocking timeout. Do not pipe interactive commands through `head`, `tail`, `grep`, or `tee`; they can wait for process exit and stall.

input.description: Optional text written verbatim to the command's stdin immediately after spawn, up to 16 KiB. Include a trailing newline for line-oriented prompts. Omit when not needed; an empty string means no input. For pty=true this is typed into the terminal: closing the writer does not send EOF, so a program that reads until EOF will wait for timeout; send `\u0004` (Ctrl-D) explicitly for that case. Do not send secrets; the text becomes part of the tool call history.

pty.description: Required: always supply this field (the call is rejected if omitted). Use true only for interactive CLIs (prompts, QR codes, full-screen UI); use false for everything else, including background commands. With `yield_time_ms`, `pty=true` starts a persistent PTY session controlled through `command_session`.

yield_time_ms.description: Start a persistent command session and wait up to this many milliseconds for output (5000-60000, default 30000). Returns a session id when the process is still running or has buffered output left to read; a command that finishes and drains inside the yield returns its output directly. Use this for servers, REPLs, and multi-step interactive commands, not builds or tests.
